subject: Re: Dedicated GPU reservation — MAP, pricing, and burst terms
messages:
From: Cormac O'Neill <cormac@orbitlabs.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated GPU reservation — initial questions and MAP request

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput looked promising for our vector search and retrieval-heavy workflows. Our engineering and procurement teams asked me to pull together a mutual action plan (MAP) so we can align evaluation milestones with a committed reservation. A few asks from our side: 

- Can you confirm a recommended GPU pool size for 30 inference workers (80k tokens/hr average per worker) and expected p99 latency targets?
- We'd like a 12-month committed term with a 3-month ramp (phased activation). What discount tiers do you offer for a 12-month commit vs a 24-month commit?
- Important: we need a documented burst clause to cover peak events up to 2.5x baseline for short windows without breaking SLA. What are the economics for burst usage?
- Please include a draft MAP spreadsheet we can iterate on and an early SOW to circulate to procurement.

If you can send the MAP and a ballpark commercial outline by the end of the week, I can brief procurement and legal.

Thanks,
Cormac O'Neill
Head of ML Platforms
Orbit Labs

Attachments: none

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Cormac O'Neill <cormac@orbitlabs.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU reservation — initial questions and MAP request

Cormac —

Appreciate the clear asks. I put together an initial MAP and commercial outline attached ("Orbit_MAP_v1.xlsx") and a starter SOW for procurement. Key high-level answers below; details in the MAP:

- Recommended pool: 8 x A800-class GPUs (we size on token throughput and concurrency). That supports ~30 workers at your stated throughput with headroom; we provide autoscale knobs to smooth usage.
- Latency: target p50/p95/p99 of 40ms / 120ms / 240ms for typical short-chat sequences; heavy-long sequences see higher tail. We include p99 SLAs in Dedicated at the enterprise tier with credit caps.
- Term & discounts: 12-month commit: 18% unit discount off list; 24-month commit: 26% off list + 90 days free credit applied at onboarding.
- Ramp: propose a 3-month staged activation: month 1 (30% capacity), month 2 (60%), month 3 (100%). Each milestone gates the next discount tranche.
- Burst: we offer two burst mechanisms (1) short-term on-demand burst billed at 1.4x committed unit rate up to 2x baseline for <6 hours/day, and (2) pre-agreed emergency burst pool at 2.5x baseline billed at 1.8x committed rate for controlled windows — both with usage caps and reporting. Details + examples in MAP.

I also included a sample mutual action plan with milestones, owners, and acceptance criteria. If procurement is comfortable, we can move to an SOW + DocuSign link for signature.

Next step: can you share the primary procurement contact (I see procurement@orbitlabs.com on copy) and preferred SOW approver? We can revise rates if Orbit wants to trade a longer term or higher minimum IOUs.

Thanks — attaching files.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Orbit_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with milestones; pricing scenarios), SOW-draft-Orbit-ORB-4921.pdf (starter SOW)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:46:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated GPU reservation — MAP, pricing, and burst terms

Hi Marcus, Laura — forwarding Cormac's ask and my draft MAP. Quick internal thread to confirm commercial posture before sending the formal SOW to procurement.

Summary of ask: 12mo commit, 3mo ramp, burst up to 2.5x baseline. They want pricing/discounts and explicit burst economics.

Proposed outbound (what I included):
- Recommend 8 A800 GPUs (sized conservatively).
- 12mo = 18% off; 24mo = 26% off + 90d credit.
- Burst options: on-demand @1.4x for short spikes (<6h/day) or emergency pool @1.8x for controlled bursts (detailed caps).
- MAP milestones: Eval completion & perf acceptance (week 4), Security review signoff (week 6), Production cutover readiness (week 12). Each milestone unlocks the next billing tranche and commit enforcement.

Questions for you:
1) Are the discount levels and burst multipliers acceptable? 18% for 12mo is slightly generous given their projected usage. We could tighten to 15% and offer an add-on credit if they sign within 30 days.
2) Do we want to require a 60% minimum-usage ramp commitment by month 2 to reduce churn risk?
3) Should we include a defined overage cap (e.g., 250% monthly max) beyond which we automatically throttle or require emergency approval?

Marcus — can you advise on the viability of the emergency burst pool from an ops standpoint and whether 1.8x committed rate covers marginal infra cost + priority scheduling?

Laura — any procurement clauses we should proactively add (early-termination, audit rights) to protect Redwood?

Thanks — if we can finalize internal posture today, I will incorporate changes and send the updated SOW + docu sign link to procurement by EOD tomorrow.

-- Tessa

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated GPU reservation — MAP, pricing, and burst terms

Quick take:
- Discount: move 12mo to 15% with a 45-day signature bonus of a one-time credits pool equal to 5% of first-year committed spend. Keeps list pricing integrity while giving procurement something immediate.
- Ramp commitment: yes — require min 60% of committed baseline by end of month 2, or we move to a reduced discount schedule (fall back to 10% for the remainder). Add a simple true-up clause at month 3.
- Burst: emergency pool at 1.8x is fine but tighten the caps — emergency burst limited to 120 GPU-hours/month and requires 24-hour notice where possible. On-demand burst stays at 1.4x with daily caps (no more than 6h/day). If they exceed monthly cap, additional usage billed at 2.2x and subject to quota reviews.
- Ops note: we can support the emergency pool but we should add a lead time SLA for enabling reserved emergency nodes (4 business hours for activation).
- Procurement clauses: Laura to confirm, but suggest explicit audit rights, data residency pointers, and a 90-day cure period for any material breach before termination.

Laura — please confirm language and I will update the SOW. If agreed, Tessa please send revised MAP + SOW and include DocuSign link.

Marcus

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Cormac O'Neill <cormac@orbitlabs.com>, procurement@orbitlabs.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU reservation — MAP, pricing, and burst terms

Cormac / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We've incorporated internal feedback and attached an updated MAP and SOW. Highlights of the revised commercial: 

- Pool sizing: same recommendation — 8 x A800-class GPUs.
- Pricing: 12-month commitment = 15% off list + one-time onboarding credits equal to 5% of first-year committed spend if signed within 45 days. 24-month remains at 26% + 90 days credit (unchanged).
- Ramp: 3-month staged activation (30% / 60% / 100%) with a required minimum of 60% of baseline by end of month 2. If not met, discount schedule reverts to 10% for the remainder of the term with a true-up at month 3.
- Burst: two mechanisms — on-demand burst at 1.4x (max 6h/day) and emergency burst pool at 1.8x (cap 120 GPU-hours/month). Emergency pool activation has a 4-business-hour lead time and requires approval; exceeding monthly cap billed at 2.2x.
- Other: 90-day cure period on material breach, audit rights, and standard data residency language in the SOW.

I've attached the updated documents and a DocuSign link to the SOW for Orbit's approver: https://app.docu.sign/ORB-4921/SOW-v1

Next steps:
1) Please confirm procurement contact and preferred approver for the SOW.
2) If acceptable, we can kick off security questionnaire (we'll assign Monica as the security lead) and schedule the first acceptance run (week 4).

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Orbit_MAP_v1.xlsx (revised), SOW-draft-Orbit-ORB-4921.pdf (updated)
